📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games employees have voted against official recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers Union, with 93.2 percent of staff participating in the vote.
  • 25 percent of those who participated voted to recognise the union, while 75 percent voted against.
  • Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing at Rockstar Games told Eurogamer: "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games employees have voted against official recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers Union, with 93.2 percent of staff participating in the vote.

25 percent of those who participated voted to recognise the union, while 75 percent voted against. If it had been approved, it would have been the largest recognised union in the UK video game industry by a large margin. While the union will still exist and organise, Rockstar Games will not have to recognise the union as a representing body for staff at the studio, and is not obligated to attend regular meetings with the body.

Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing at Rockstar Games told Eurogamer: "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

The Rockstar Union also released a statement following the outcome of this vote, saying Rockstar employees will continue to organise despite the lack of recognition. It reads:.

According to recent reports, "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

Recent findings suggest that "A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against Al and layoffs.

"The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.".

Sources indicate that rockstar employees represented by the union are still awaiting the verdict from the Rockstar Games vs IWGB employment tribunal legal case, of which the final verdict is still pending. This case was kicked off by the sudden firing of employees present in a union Discord server. The employees claim this was an attempt at union busting by Rockstar, while the organization denies this, saying it was for breaking confidentiality agreements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yellowjackets, the time-hopping survival drama about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive, is coming to an end. Whether or not it sticks the landing, it's been one helluva ride, and we'll soon have room in the streaming schedule for other other highlights about young people having a pretty rough go of it while just trying to survive.

Sources indicate that situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It promptly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, not just a show about girlfights. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that A bit more grounded...but only at first glance, The Stranded takes place on a Thai island in the midst of a tsunami. The island was formerly home to a prestigious high school, and a bunch of students have snuck back for an ill-timed party on the last day of class. A bad idea, clearly, after the storm hits. Kraam (Papangkorn Lerkchaleampote), one of the few students who actually lives on the island, is trapped there along with a couple dozen classmates. Kraam knows the island, but Anan (Chutavuth Pattarakampol) assumes leadership while other students either take on necessary roles or fall in line. As the miniseries progresses, the upcoming social order breaks down, even as the island's mysteries reveal themselves and things get weirder and more complex. Stream The Stranded on Netflix.

According to recent reports, A handful of influencers get invited to a remote island, which is obviously a very good thing to agree to that will not lead to dramatic complications in any way. Behind the neon-lit party vibes, there's a cult at work and some ritualistic shenanigans with deadly consequences. Eden is more concerned with the survival horror than with some of the deeper themes and mysteries of Yellowjackets, but we're still playing with shifting power dynamics in this Spanish import. Stream Welcome to Eden on Netflix.

The premise of The Leftovers is brilliantly subdued: Around two percent of the world's population disappears without explanation, and it's enough to upend just about everything. Politics have adapted to the new normal, religions have collapsed and reformed, and families have had to make peace with the inexplicable loss of loved ones. The first season revolves around the Garvey family, led by Kevin (Justin Theroux), a sheriff whose wife (Amy Brenneman) left him to join a cult, while subsequent seasons broaden the scope to bring in other characters in other locations. It's more philosophical than Yellowjackets, and quieter, but the indicates share an interest in the lingering effects of trauma, and in the stuff we get up to under threat and in the dark. Stream The Leftovers on HBO Max.

The 100 tells the story of the descendants of refugees of nuclear devastation who return to Earth from their habitat in space to encounter the remnants of humanity who have survived on Earth. Naturally, the first people sent to scope things out are the juvenile delinquents (better them than me), and they discover that three civilizations have risen up in the aftermath of the apocalypse, and they are all pretty scary (including one populated by cannibals, naturally). More sci-fi than horror, but the survivalist themes and mysteries here make it more than a decent match. The show builds an impressive mythology over the course of its run, leading to a conclusion that’s borderline metaphysical. Stream The 100 on Pluto TV or buy it from Prime Video.

When pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

A massive apocalyptic tidal wave strikes during the 10-year reunion of the graduating class of an all-girls high school. The event leaves them all trapped together (a nightmare in any event), and forced to survive while reliving old struggles and dramas. It's Yellowjackets-esque, absolutely, but also Australian and a comedy, which doesn't feel like as much of a stretch as you'd think given the over-the-top nature of that show. Stream Class of '07 on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that A remote, charming town with some deep, dark secrets (the biggest of which, and one that it shares with Yellowjackets, is rather strongly hinted in the title), Gannibal stars Yuya Yagira as Daigo Agawa, a police officer from the significant city who takes a job in the super cute (and, of course, remote) village of Kuge following some personal trouble. The perfectly charming Goto family runs the town, more or less, and welcomes Daigo and his family. It's all looking pretty great—until a mysterious man gives Daigo's daughter a severed finger as a gift, and his wife Yuki finds the words "Run Away" scrawled over a door in their newly introduced home. Just a couple of reasons why I'm more of a city person. Stream Gannibal on Disney+ and Hulu.

This latter-day plane crash narrative goes all-in on mystery and philosophy, virtually pioneering the timey-wimey reveal format that makes Yellowjackets so juicy. We kick off with flashbacks that peel back the layers of the various crash survivors before diving headfirst into warm-weather polar bears and mysterious underground bunkers and monsters made of smoke. Whether it's an uncommonly smart network show that rewards careful viewing or a load of nonsense is in the eye of the beholder—but it remains one of the most discussed and debated reveals in TV history. Stream Lost on Disney+ and Hulu.

Kathryn Newton heads this surprisingly smart Lord of the Flies riff about a group of teenagers forced to create their own community after all the adults disappear and a dense new forest crops up around their small enclave, cutting them off from everything and everyone else. This one's about coming of age in a world where the usual rules are no longer in effect, and about how we're quick to reestablish an oppressive social order even when outside forces are no longer at work. Stream The Society on Netflix.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Over its first seven days on sale, GTA 6 has amassed over 420m hours watched, according to Streams Charts.
  • As for the livestreaming platforms that saw the largest audiences for GTA 6, YouTube reportedly had the lead in average audience numbers during the first six hours of launch, but Twitch took over in content volume in the days that followed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has broken another livestreaming record. After attracting more viewers across livestreaming platforms than any game ever on its launch day, Rockstar's open-world crime sim has reportedly continued to dominate on platforms like Twitch, YouTube, and Kick.

Over its first seven days on sale, GTA 6 has amassed over 420m hours watched, according to Streams Charts. That's nearly three times more than the previous record, held by Valorant's closed beta in April 2020. In fact, that 420m hours tally is more than the first-week watch time achieved by Valorant, Elden Ring, Diablo 4, and Lost Ark combined.

As for the livestreaming platforms that saw the largest audiences for GTA 6, YouTube reportedly had the lead in average audience numbers during the first six hours of launch, but Twitch took over in content volume in the days that followed. In fact, Twitch's GTA 6 watch time was higher at launch than any other game in its history.

Streams Charts also noted 1,056 channels reached new all-time peak viewership numbers while streaming GTA 6, in some cases multiplying their previous record tenfold. Major content creators like IShowSpeed, IlloJuan, and TheBurntPeanut stole the spotlight, but GTA 6 also helped many other channels set new viewership records.

Livestreaming, of course, isn't the only area where GTA 6 has set upcoming records. Publisher Take-Two called it the biggest entertainment launch in history, generating $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue from 32.5m copies sold on day one. Other parts of the industry have benefited, too. Anticipation for GTA 6 boosted US hardware sales for both PlayStation and Xbox, just as GTA 6 became each console brand's most pre-ordered title ever. At launch, more than 39 million people played GTA 6 on PS5, according to Sony. The game also had the highest number of concurrent players ever on any PlayStation console, beating even the most popular free-to-play titles.

According to recent reports, you can check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough if you're in need of assistance, which we just updated today with a guide on how to whistle in GTA 6 - something I didn't know you could do. The walkthrough also covers other lesser-known mechanics such as how to steal ATMs in GTA 6, and much more besides.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that despite being set in the past, WoW: Forever is an attempt to capture the spirit of the old game by injecting it with newly introduced quirks that challenge new and returning players alike to approach it differently than any other version of the MMO. This is why familiar old dungeons can drop new loot, like an armor set that turns you into a snake.

It has been revealed that blizzard has stated that its goal is to "unsolve" the game as best it can so players don't settle into the same routines they're used to. This is especially true for min-maxed strategies that threaten to suck the fun out of enjoying the game, or "the journey", as Blizzard likes to call it.

It's a lofty goal that can't be achieved without persistently fiddling with the knobs that encourage players to do one thing over another—which is the very thing that differentiates WoW: Forever from WoW Classic.

Sources indicate that this week, Blizzard stepped in to fix a problem that was brewing in its 40-player MOBA-esque PvP mode Alterac Valley. Players were avoiding PvP altogether, turning it into a glorified reputation farm.

"We’ve seen that players in Alterac Valley were frequently completing the battleground without capturing the objectives, so we’ve made some adjustments to incentivize a focus on the objectives rather than rushing to kill the enemy faction’s general," community manager Kaivax wrote.

Industry observers note that the patch basically broke a popular 'zerg' strategy where one side rushed to end the match as fast as possible by beefing up the NPC defenders that stood in their way. Blizzard shifted some of the reputation and honor you'd normally get from killing the generals to the other objectives so players are encouraged to engage with the whole mode.

According to recent reports, but, as I've seen with changes like this in the past few weeks, many players are upset that they can't just spam it for the rewards, and that others have already reaped the benefits of the old strategy. There are people in Reddit threads doing the math to highlight how much efficiency has been lost (it doesn't seem like much) and questioning the point of doing Alterac Valley at all.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

While I sympathize with not wanting to do something that feels like a chore, it's a far worse problem to have an entire part of the game flattened into an AFK farm. Alterac Valley is supposed to feel like a large-scale war where you look at a big map and choose what objectives are worth fighting over as you try to weaken the enemy forces. The loot you get from maxing out your reputation with the associated factions is meant to be a reward for putting in the effort to learn what it takes to win.

Sources indicate that the whole pitch for WoW: Forever is that it's not going to ditch everything with a upcoming expansion every few years. Numbers can be tweaked down the line if the reputation grind is too much of a slog, but the mode should be fun to play so it's not treated like a box to check off in your character's journey. An inert PvP mode ruins the spirit of the MMO far more than a slightly longer reputation grind does.

It has been revealed that I think this is a good example of a healthy change that indicates Blizzard is committed to protecting core parts of the experience from becoming a treadmill that nobody enjoys. WoW: Forever's strengths are the ways it encourages you to participate in systems that aren't there to fill progression bars. As Harvey said in his WoW: Forever review, "Forever is proof that old-school MMO design deserves a second chance," and that requires taking a stance on what the game is and isn't meant to be.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that among the many, many side activities you can do in GTA 6, there's powerwashing. Relatively early on, as part of Chapter 1's Down to Earth mission, Jason whips out his nozzle and blasts Brian's boat to a gleaming sheen. Disappointingly for powerwashing fans, though, it's a bit of a one-and-done gag, never to return. But powerwashing is powerwashing, and we immediately wondered what the experts made of it all. Had Rockstar, with its legendary attention to detail, accurately captured the intricacies of powerwashing in those leisurely moments of carefree squirting?

According to recent reports, A question had been asked and an answer was required. So who better to cast judgement on the authenticity of Jason's sway-and-spraying than FuturLab, the studio behind the delightfully zen PowerWash Simulator series? Thus, in a moment of whimsy, I asked if it might like to 'review' GTA 6's hosiest activity. At best, I was hoping for a cheeky little statement; I certainly wasn't expecting a significant chunk of the PowerWash Simulator 2 team to join in the fun. "Fair to say," the intermediary PR noted, "the Futurlab team was excited about this one!".

According to recent reports, so what's the verdict? Let us turn to the pros. "They've got the sounds and satisfaction of clearly a nice shiny flat surface just right," PowerWash Simulator 2 lead game designer Nick McCarthy opined, "but where's the ding!? 0/10, needs 200 percent more layers of muck and 20 percent more parkour." And rapidly a trend emerged. "Great visuals, satisfying feel, but lacks the crucial ding and went by too quickly to listen to a podcast," senior programmer Will Dyball wrote. Then still more sadness for the lack of PowerWash Simulator's most motivating sound: "Didn't hear a ding," associate publishing producer Jess Crosby wrote. "Must have missed a bit.".

A few team members also spotted some powerwashing faux pas. "No soap?" wrote 3D artist Eilidh Norris. "Rookie mistake, Jason." Programmer Jordan Lewis also reckoned Jason was making things unnecessarily hard for himself: "[He'd] have had an easier time had he taken the time to upgrade his washer and purchased some more nozzles," they wrote. "PS. Soap would have gotten that off in a flash." Others had safety concerns: "I find Jason's lack of protective overalls disturbing," said 3D artist Rory Peace, and data principal Russell Young agreed. "Clean speedboat, ruined clothes. Don't want to bring them 'Down to Earth', but we need to talk about PPE." People advisor Sarah Robshaw, meanwhile, spotted a more heinous omission: "Where's the cats????".

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, game designer Sam Jenkins was delighted by the powerwashing representation. "I'm so glad that the Art of Powerwashing is being taken more seriously in mainstream games!" they wrote. "However, I think the dirt on the boat is too scarce for that satisfying cleaning contrast to come through.".

It has been revealed that jenkins even had some expert suggestions to make Jason's little squirt-out more rewarding: "Maybe the boat should have been left in a flooded warehouse for 30 years to coat it in grime?" they continued. "Or even have a crushed fruit festival come through town to get some nice big colourful blobs all over the boat. Ooh! And we could even have the boat be the home of various squids to get some difficult-to-clean Ink streaked down it too!" Truly the words of someone who takes their powerwashing seriously!

Recent findings suggest that junior build engineer Owen Layton, programmer Jordan Lewis, and lead designer Nick McCarthy also provided 'reviews' in pictoral form, but technical complications mean they'll just have to exist in your imagination. Senior narrative designer Mark Ginbey, though, expressed admiration for all the in-world encouragement players are given. "Some excellent motivational text updates from Cal, like 'Mmhmm, half way there...' to indicate 50 percent completion," they wrote. "But Jason needs to concentrate on the work in hand. A quality powerwasher never talks on the job.".

Senior game designer António Salreta had praise for GTA 6, with one exception: "It's an amazing game with so many fun systems - but. Needs. More. Nozzles." And how's this for a ringing endorsement from senior QA tester Paul Comse? "I love coming home after a hard day of work powerwashing in PowerWash Sim and unwinding by powerwashing some more in GTA," they wrote. But if we're scoring Jason's efforts? "7.8/10, too much water.".

So there you go! The experts have spoken, and I'd call it a success for Rockstar's inaugural attempt at powerwashing, despite a handful of 'must try harders'. An unexpectedly generous response indeed! And if you're curious how FuturLab does it, look no further than last year's PowerWash Simulator 2. And for help with powerwashing in GTA 6, we've got a guide.

A SIDE A child is born in 1989 and grows up on a Christmas tree farm south of Reading, Pennsylvania. She is destined for the stage. At 15, she signs with a newly opened record label in Nashville. It’s soon clear that she’s a generational talent. Her name foretells her future fate: the Latin root of celebrity is celere, meaning “rapid,” “fast,” “swift.”.

She has romantic associations with celebrities—some of whom treat her ­badly, including a member of a boy band who breaks up with her over a 27-second phone call. By that pOint, she is a celebrity herself. But fame has not warped her the way it has nearly everybody else: She doesn’t even have a manager! What she has are her many great friends. She tells them everything and is pleasantly surprised when they do not put her on blast.

Industry observers note that at 29, the record manufacturer from Nashville betrays her by selling her life’s work to her archnemesis’s manager. She would have bought the rights to her own songs, only she was never afforded the chance. The sale between the two men occurs without her knowing. When she finds out, she appeals to her loyal fans, who defend her in her moral outrage. With their support, she wins the rights to her music. By then, she’s met her shining knight. After a happy and very public courtship, your English and your gym teachers wed.

When the curtain falls on humanity, they will say that for a time, she defined American sonic life—that her music owned the ’10s and the long ’20s.

Recent findings suggest that B SIDE A child is born and grows up on an 11-acre Christmas tree farm that her third-generation banker father bought from a client at Merrill Lynch, where he is a vice president and manages a portfolio around $270 million. When she is 10 years old, the family moves to a 3,560-square-foot, five-bedroom, three-and-a-half-bath Georgian Colonial in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania. A visitor calls the house a “six-star hotel.”.

Her mOther is “definitely a theater mom, very aggressive,” says Sandy Carbone, whose son directs The Star in Grease, Bye Bye Birdie, The Sound of Music. The mom asks Carbone’s other son, a computer repairman named Ronnie Cremer, if he might teach her daughter to play a 12-string guitar. “She used to complain a lot about the guitar chords,” Cremer says, “that it hurt her hands.” Cremer relays this to the parents. “Just keep worKing her,” they reply. “She needs this to get better.”.

Once, during a lesson, the mother returns home with Taco Bell. The girl, who is not yet a star, scampers to the kitchen, but salad is her lot. “Nobody wants to see a fat pop star,” Cremer recalls the mother saying. (Cremer first told the Newly introduced York Daily News this story in 2015. The Star declined to comment then. Vanity Fair sent The Star multiple questions while reporting this story; she declined to comment.).

Her father’s connections lead to his daughter singing the national anthem before a minor league baseball game, which leads to another performance, which he videotapes and sends to a marketing manager for the Philadelphia 76ers. Which is how she ends up singing the national anthem for them, wearing red, white, and blue.

It has been revealed that four months into her guitar-playing career, according to Cremer, her father begins driving his daughter to various gigs, giving away tickets to business associates and other acquaintances. Cremer says her father asks that they cheer his daughter loudly so she always seems to be playing to a full house. He captures these performances on tape to send to Nashville, before moving the family there.

Sources indicate that her fame grows. She becomes a Star. Her erstwhile suitors grouse that the songs she writes about them are misrepresentations—that their relationship lasted only a few weeks, or that the call was 27 seconds because she hung up first. In lieu of a manager, what The Star has is her mother and a closed board of stakeholders. Her many friends do not dare speak ill of her—dare not speak of her at all.

By 2006 the father has a stake in the Nashville record company, after making a financial investment worth a reported $500,000, according to Music Business Worldwide. He makes $15 million when it sells. In 2023 she becomes a billionaire on account of her tour, the highest grossing of all time. Her fans do not mind. “Of all the billionaires,” a fan notes, “she is my favorite billionaire!”.

When the curtain falls on humanity, they will say that for a time she defined American sonic life—that her music owned the ’10s and the long ’20s.

She is a wedding reception for 1,000 and $26 million to charity for the inconvenience to any. She says vote and tens of thousands register. She wears a bandeau “nap top” and midi skirt, and everyone else buys a bandeau nap top and midi skirt. She is our most gracious homecoming queen, our Miss Americana. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has had a huge effect on physical game sales in the UK, despite not actually containing a disc in the box.

NielsenIQ data shows that GTA 6 drove boxed software sales up an enormous 409 percent for the launch period ending 21st November, compared to the previous week, resulting in the biggest week for UK physical game sales since Christmas 2018.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 alone accounted for £32m of the total £43m boxed software sales, apparently - around 74 percent, with 88 percent of its sales generated on day-one. But it's not a champion or record-breaker in this regard. In fact, GTA 6 places 17th in the all-time table of first-week boxed revenue, which is refreshingly humbling given the money-making records it's been breaking elsewhere. This is to do with the overwhelming shift towards buying games digitally, of course.

Nevertheless, Rockstar is well represented in the all-time list (which stretches back to 1995), because it's none other than GTA 5 that sits at the top, and GTA 4 at 11th.

Sources indicate that but the GTA 6 effect is that of a rising tide, with console hardware sales rising 38 percent, to their highest level since 2025. Specifically, PS5 sales rose 46 percent and Xbox Series sales jumped a considerable 75 percent. And it's been a similar result in the US, where PS5 and Xbox Series sales have more than doubled.

Gaming accessory sales also got a boost, with PS5 controller sales up 355 percent, gaming headset sales up 94 percent, and - more nichely - gaming chair sales up 32 percent, which is apparently in line with the 40 percent increase they experienced around GTA 5.

"While the physical games market looks very different today compared with previous blockbuster introduces, GTA 6 has still made a huge impact," stated NielsenIQ's Dorian Bloch. "Back in 2008, boxed software accounted for half of all games retail revenue for the combined sectors of software, hardware, and gaming accessories, compared with 15 percent so far in 2026. This is a reflection of the market increasingly shifting towards digital downloads.".

It's against this backdrop, of course, that Sony made its hugely controversial decision to wind down production of PlayStation game discs starting January 2028. This has led to boycotts and backlash and much angry sentiment towards the company, but Grand Theft Auto 6's enormous digital success is likely to be a hard example to ignore.

If You Loved 'Cupertino,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cupertino is one of those TV reveals that arrived just when we all needed it.
  • Sources indicate that just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not.
  • According to recent reports, at its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cupertino is one of those TV reveals that arrived just when we all needed it. In this economy, a story about two lawyers who get shafted by the “move fast and break things” culture of Silicon Valley and decide to use their legal chops to fight back was almost destined to be a hit, and the great performances by Mike Colter and Rachel Keller sealed the deal. If you love the sharp legal wrangling and tech-focused storylines and want a movie that perfectly complements the show, it’s time to watch (or re-watch) Aaron Sorkin and David Fincher’s 2010 masterpiece, The Social Network.

Sources indicate that just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not. While it might seem hard to imagine, there was a time when Facebook was the social media platform—everyone was on it, and it dominated the conversation like nothing else. And the outsized wealth and influence Zuckerberg accrued as a result were just starting to make people a little uneasy.

According to recent reports, at its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s. Like Cupertino, the story is soaked in the “apologize later” culture of tech startups, and traces the ruthlessness and cold genius of Zuckerberg as he cements his control over the platform, ices out former partners, and generally behaves like a sociopathic genius (Jesse Eisenberg’s performance as Zuckerberg is coldly compelling).

Sources indicate that the film doesn’t have any kind of clear-cut ending where the good guys win, but there’s a certain satisfaction in the way Sorkin’s script and Eisenberg’s performance strip away the glamour of Zuckerberg’s money and success, reducing him in many ways to an aggrieved loner who translated his rage into a brilliant idea, and then has to isolate himself from everyone in order to maintain his control over it. The Zuckerberg depicted in the film is a lonely, bitter dude, and it’s as much of a happy ending as you’ll get. It’s a fascinating story of legal maneuvering and bickering lawyers against a backdrop of one of the foundational social media moments that shaped modern culture, and fans of the show will dig it. Stream The Social Network on Pluto or rent it on Prime Video.

Still craving legal drama, tech-sector skulduggery, or more David-versus-Goliath courtroom fireworks? Here are a few more movies that fans of Cupertino will love.

It’s set nowhere near Silicon Valley, but Michael Clayton is a real barn-burner of a paranoid legal thriller. George Clooney plays the title role, a “fixer” for a big-money law firm. When his mentor and friend, Arthur Edens (Tom Wilkinson), suffers a mental breakdown while working on a case involving a toxic weedkiller produced by one of the firm’s clients and becomes a security threat, he’s assassinated, and Clayton is forced to reckon with his role in the world and how much injustice he’s willing to tolerate in exchange for money. It’s tense, smart, and has a wonderfully satisfying conclusion that fans of legal dramas where the good guys are willing to sacrifice (and win) will cheer. Rent Michael Clayton on Prime Video.

Based on real events, Dark Waters will appeal to anyone who likes to see smart lawyers take on enormous corporations in a search for the truth. A successful corporate lawyer, Robert Bilott (Mark Ruffalo), looks into a series of bizarre cattle deaths in rural West Virginia and stumbles onto evidence that the DuPont corporation has been dumping illegal, unregulated chemicals into the groundwater. Bilott’s years-long effort to hold DuPont responsible for the health impact on the community nearly costs him everything, but his determination to make the system work is ultimately the kind of inspiring legal story fans of Cupertino will appreciate. Rent Dark Waters on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that if you just want the simple pleasures of a thrilling legal procedural, you can’t do much better than A Civil Action. John Travolta (at the height of his comeback) plays attorney Jan Schlichtmann, who takes on a class action lawsuit against two huge corporations because he thinks the case will be lucrative and relatively straightforward. As the case saps his resources and brings his firm to the brink of collapse, however, Schlichtmann slowly realizes that he’s fighting for more than just a major payday. Fair warning: This isn’t a feel-good movie in many ways, but it definitely brings those David-versus-Goliath vibes that Cupertino trades in. Rent A Civil Action on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that the true story behind the effort to license the video game Tetris from the Soviet-era Russian government doesn’t have the same stakes as many of the stories in Cupertino, and it’s certainly no longer timely. But the globe-trotting legal maze that Henk Rogers (Taron Egerton) must navigate to secure the rights, which seem to keep twisting and slipping from his grasp as various political and corporate interests weigh in, is just as fun and fascinating as the legal battles on the show. Tetris may no longer be a novel sensation in the gaming world, but it’s fascinating to see how something so baked into modern pop culture achieved that status. Stream Tetris on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If your favorite part of Cupertino is its exploration of the way tech companies impact our lives, and the way decisions made in obscure corporate offices can have enormous consequences, BlackBerry will be a favorite. Based on true events, it tells the story of how Research in Motion (RIM) created what was, for a time, the most dominant phone in the world—and how the manufacturer lost everything when its leaders took their eye off the ball and let personal obsessions and grudges impede their work. With a cast that includes Jay Baruchel and Glenn Howerton, this story of Silicon Valley hubris is right on target for Cupertino fans. Stream Blackberry on Netflix, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that microsoft-owned developer platform Github stepped in it earlier today when it posted a message on X celebrating the success of AnyPS5, an open source project that aims to let users port PS5 executables to PC, and then linked that success directly to efforts to port Grand Theft Auto 6 to PC. The message was deleted shortly after it was posted, but not before it was widely noticed and called out for being a very bad idea.

"GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on Github," the message stated (via Kotaku).

"The repo AnyPS5 has passed 58K stars since its August launch, rewriting PS5 executables to run on Windows and Linux. Does changing where games run cross a legal line? Share your take. Happy GTA VImas!".

According to recent reports, lest there be any misunderstanding, a video that accompanied the post made the GTA 6 connection explicit: "The project rewrites a game's executable so Windows and Linux can run it directly. Performance seems to be the main problem for people wanting to run GTA 6, with one contributor telling the project's community to 'lock in and get your agents to help' if they need to.".

And here's the accompanying video from @github's GTA6 tweet https://t.co/crU9cpOWcsNovember 26, 2026.

In a recent development, the question of whether or not this sort of thing crosses a legal line has, predictably, sparked debate among those who think they have a clear understanding of the answer. What caught most by surprise, though, is that Github—which is owned by Microsoft—would put forth the question in the first place, implicitly suggesting that it might not. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive has been pretty aggressive with its efforts to keep recompiled versions of GTA 6 from landing on PC, and I can't imagine it would too thrilled with Github—which, I must emphasize, is owned by Microsoft—telling the world that it might actually be okay to go ahead and vibe-code it up.

It has been revealed that that point wasn't missed by redditors, one of whom described it as Github "openly taunting Sony and Rockstar." Even the AnyPS5 subreddit seemed baffled: Redditor superkickstart asked, "Do they have AI running their socials? Lol".

There's also a little bit of irony in the fact that, until earlier this week, the leading effort to get GTA 6 running on PC was based on an Xbox build of the game posted by GTA 6 leaker Cyberleeks. Beyond that, there are also some very obvious questions about how Github (owned by Microsoft) would react to AI-powered ports of, say, other software:.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In a recent development, the whole thing is weird, really, because it seems like such an obviously bad idea. The only explanation I can come up with is that a social media manager either didn't think about it, didn't understand it (which would be weird in itself for someone doing social media posts for Github), or just had a substantial ol' brain fart. Whatever the reason, I imagine someone got a good old-fashioned talking-to about it.

I've reached out to Github and Take-Two for comment and will revision if I receive a reply.

In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry. Go to Hyde Island Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out. Listen to your captor's speech Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move. Run to the tent directly in front of you You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers. Search for more outposts You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you. Prepare for a showdown Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off. Collect your rewards Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work. What happens if you fail? If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again. Nioh and Ninja Gaiden studio is using AI for QA, but argues "that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Team Ninja (Nioh, Ninja Gaiden) is the latest game development studio to implement AI into some of its workflow, but producer Kohei Shibata still believes that fun games need to be "crafted by human hands.".
  • Sources indicate that the producer best known for the tough-as-nails Nioh trilogy and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty spoke about the controversial tech during South Korea's GCON 2026, in an interview with INVEN Global.
  • He went on to argue that if AI can "shorten task times," then developers can spend more hours "elevating the game's overall quality" in other ways.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Ninja (Nioh, Ninja Gaiden) is the latest game development studio to implement AI into some of its workflow, but producer Kohei Shibata still believes that fun games need to be "crafted by human hands.".

Sources indicate that the producer best known for the tough-as-nails Nioh trilogy and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty spoke about the controversial tech during South Korea's GCON 2026, in an interview with INVEN Global. "Currently, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows," Shibata explained.

He went on to argue that if AI can "shorten task times," then developers can spend more hours "elevating the game's overall quality" in other ways. "In that sense, using AI is beneficial." Team Ninja isn't fully on board with enforcing the tech elsewhere, though: "Since it's still a latest technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions." (Good spot, Kotaku.).

Sources indicate that "What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future," Shibata continued.

According to recent reports, generative AI's use in game development is still a hotly debated topic among both players and the people making games, but it's been prevalent nonetheless. A recent report estimated that around 40 percent of game developers were using AI in some fashion, even if lots of them also agreed the tech was harmful. Bigger publishers like Ubisoft and Epic Games are more aggressively pursuing an AI-first future, too.

Team Ninja seems to be settling into a middle ground, at least, according to Shibata's statement. Speaking on the studio's approach to difficult games, he stated that a player's failure should never be the game's fault. Dying in a game like Ninja Gaiden or Nioh should always be the result of human error, otherwise death "causes frustration." Finding that perfect, often bloody sweet spot is something only humans can do.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the holiday season upon us and the 2026 movie calendar winding down, there are a handful of the best Christmas movies I return to every December, and Elf is pretty much guaranteed to make the list. Will Ferrell running around Latest York City in yellow tights, eating spaghetti covered in candy and screaming about Santa Claus has become as much a part of the holidays as putting up the tree. According to one of the movie's stars, Hollywood wasn't exactly convinced it had a future Christmas classic on its hands back in 2003.

Recent findings suggest that andy Richter, who played Morris in the Jon Favreau-directed comedy, recently reflected on the making of Elf and explained why the movie was considered something of a gamble. Speaking with People while promoting his new book, Elf: Unwrapped, which he co-wrote with Aaron Karo, Richter noted the movie's eventual success makes it easy to forget just how uncertain things were when production began.

It was a risky movie, and nobody thinks about that because it’s now a classic, but at the time there was nobody that was aching to make a movie with Will Ferrell as the star or with Jon Favreau as the director, for that matter.

According to recent reports, considering Will Ferrell himself had doubts when he first tried on Buddy's iconic costume, I can understand why some studio executives might have been nervous. At the time, the SNL alum was best known for his work on Saturday Night Live, where he'd spent seven seasons establishing himself as one of the show's biggest stars. He'd appeared in movies like Old School and Zoolander, but he hadn't yet proven he could carry a major studio comedy as its leading man.

Sources indicate that favreau, meanwhile, had directed the 2001 comedy Made, but he was still relatively inexperienced behind the camera. According to Richter, the studio was taking a chance on both men. He added:.

They were rolling the dice with this movie and it really paid off.

It's funny to think about now, considering Ferrell went on to become one of the biggest comedy stars of the 2000s, while Favreau would eventually direct Iron Man, helping launch the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He's also had a major hand in shaping the modern Star Wars franchise with The Mandalorian. But back in 2003, the idea of giving a relatively untested leading man a Christmas comedy about a grown man raised by elves probably sounded pretty ridiculous on paper. And considering some of the behind-the-scenes stories about making Elf, it's remarkable how well everything came together. It is a ridiculous premise. That's a substantial part of why I love it.

Industry observers note that richter also credited the combination of Ferrell's comedic instincts and Favreau's approach to storytelling for making the movie work. Interestingly, though, the movie’s star recently addressed the longstanding rumors about his relationship with Favreau during the production. It seems there's still plenty to learn about what went into making this particular Christmas classic. As for Richter, he told the outlet that the film succeeds because:.

The combination of their two sensibilities, which we go into in the book, that really made it work because it’s funny, but also has a lot of heart.

I think that's a pretty accurate assessment. Ferrell gets to be completely absurd as Buddy, whether he's congratulating a coffee shop for having the world's best cup of coffee or trying to navigate a revolving door. Yet the movie also gives us a genuinely sweet story about a guy looking for his father and trying to find somewhere he belongs.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

James Caan's performance as Walter Hobbs deserves some credit here, too. His perpetually irritated reaction to Buddy's enthusiasm makes their relationship work, and without that dynamic, I don't think the movie would have nearly the same emotional payoff. Whatever reservations Hollywood had about the project, audiences certainly didn't share them once it arrived in theaters.

According to The Numbers, Elf opened to more than $31 million during its first weekend in November 2003. It has since earned approximately $234 million worldwide, including revenue from subsequent theatrical releases. That's a pretty impressive return for a movie with a reported $32 million production budget.

The movie was successful enough that Hollywood naturally wanted another one, though Ferrell has since explained why he walked away from a potentially lucrative Elf sequel.

Industry observers note that more than two decades later, it's difficult to imagine the holiday season without Buddy the Elf. The movie remains a favorite among families, and people are still finding latest things to appreciate about it, including one particularly interesting question about Buddy's journey from the North Pole to New York City.

It has been revealed that I find it interesting that a movie nobody could guarantee would succeed has become something people practically schedule their Christmas celebrations around. Ferrell has made plenty of successful comedies since, and Favreau's career has gone places nobody could have predicted in 2003.

Recent findings suggest that there's something special about Elf. Considering how many Christmas movies come and go without making much of an impression, I suspect the people who took that gamble are pretty happy they did.

Elf is streaming with a Hulu subscription.

Due to the poor ratings of the November 19 TNF game, the full-season average now for TNF games this season sank to 16.62 million on per game. One expert told GameSpot that live sports like football probably won't be too heavily impacted by GTA 6 because people want to watch in real time. The low ratings for the November 19 matchup could be partially attributable to competition with GTA 6, but a likelier scenario is that people tuned out because it was a boring game in which the heavily favored Texans throttled the Colts by a score of 26-3. The Texans were up 17-3 at the half, and the game only had nine more points total scored in the second half--all by the Texans. Not exactly thrilling stuff that people would stay glued to. Ahead of GTA 6's launch, people also wondered how The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which released on November 20, might be impacted. It may have been, but the film still put up massive numbers at the box office that exceeded expectations. GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies via pre-purchases alone and generated close to $4 billion on day one. The game will continue to sell, and it should get another jolt of sales when the PC edition arrives in 2027, as rumored. Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch.
  • Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
  • When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”.

When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

Sources indicate that dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

Recent findings suggest that the casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He states to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”.

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting new additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

According to recent reports, in Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a significant blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy showed me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she notes. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”.

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” notes Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”.

Industry observers note that villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” notes Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”.

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the major surprises in the ensemble.”.

Sources indicate that taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” says Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”.

Industry observers note that A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” states Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”.

Pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she states. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”.

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” states Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

Industry observers note that for Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most crucial for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

The Best Last-Minute Gifts That Don't Feel Last Minute

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give.
  • It has been revealed that with the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

It has been revealed that with the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

Recent findings suggest that and focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

Recent findings suggest that digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:.

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

Pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

It has been revealed that include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”.

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

Recent findings suggest that sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:.

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

SpiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

Sources indicate that mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

According to recent reports, cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

It has been revealed that sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

Flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

According to recent reports, wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

Hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

Industry News: Union Vote Fails In Landslide At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games As 75 Percent Of Devs Vote No

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (669 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games will not be forced to formally recognize a union at the Grand Theft Auto 6 studio after its developers based in the UK voted overwhelmingly against the initiative.
  • Industry observers note that voting began on November 12 and concluded today on November 26.
  • Industry observers note that “We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement shared with Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Rockstar GamesUnion.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games will not be forced to formally recognize a union at the Grand Theft Auto 6 studio after its developers based in the UK voted overwhelmingly against the initiative. The weeks-long voting process played out as Rockstar launched the open-world hit to over 30 million sales in its first day.

Industry observers note that voting began on November 12 and concluded today on November 26. Workers at Rockstar Games voted 75 percent against the recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. The initiate would have formalized collective bargaining efforts around things like overtime, bonuses, layoffs, and AI. Developers in favor of unionizing can still work with the IGWB, but there will be no regular meetings with management to hash out latest policies.

Industry observers note that “We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement shared with Kotaku. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.â.

The IWGB Game Workers Union pushing the vote released the following statement:.

For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isnât a sign to retreat, itâs a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. Weâre ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

According to recent reports, whilst we havenât emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

In a recent development, A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But itâs one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. Weâll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.

The vote comes roughly a year after Rockstar fired dozens of developers it accused of gross misconduct and breaking confidentiality rules around the development of GTA 6. The fired workers accused the studio of union busting, which it has denied, and a legal fight has been ongoing over the last 12 months at a labor tribunal. A final judgement in that case is still pending. As recently as this month, members of both sides of the dispute were testifying on the record for the case.

"Two things are certain in a witcher's life: the Path never sleeps, and the work is never done," the studio wrote in its latest exhaustive list of patch notes for the decade-old game.

Patch 5.02's handiest changes come from those aforementioned bug fixes, many of which once caused the game to crash entirely or simply not work as intended. One such bug caused "time to go backwards indefinitely." Another turned Geralt bald. Opening the game with outdated mods could also result in a crash on PC. Recent findings suggest that when The Witcher 3 Remastered first dropped, many players also took concern with the game's updated and sometimes "lifeless" lighting. Previous CDPR patches already targeted the lighting changes in question, but this newest patch continues to fix "various lighting complications across multiple locations and cutscenes.".

The studio specifically names "overly bright or dark areas" and "inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering.".

Recent findings suggest that the Witcher 3's free remastered upgrade also gave all console owners access to mod support, though not all pre-existing PC mods were available to download for console folks. This patch is expanding the selection somewhat with 40 new cross-platform mods, including glowy eyes for Geralt and a new monster hunt - and on social media, the studio promised "more on the way.".

Industry observers note that CD Projekt Red is still hard at work on two significant upcoming sequels, The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2. Speaking on the former in a recent earnings call, joint-CEO Michal Nowakowski stated we can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as we've just seen from GTA 5 to GTA 6.

The fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low. Thursday Night Football also saw a substantial dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's upcoming open-world adventure can't be blamed entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120 million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. 💡 Key Takeaways
